assertion_audit.tests/test_a_ledger_load_stats_no_run_fi: The positive control fails if os.stat interception misses a known file; the population check fails on dropped identities; reinstating the file-backed loader reddens the zero-stat assertion (reproduction.log records 800).

A missed JSON interception fails the positive control; losing plan selection returns extra identities; returning stored wall_seconds=1 or computing width from the single selected row fails the independent 3600/200 literals; decoding unrelated rows fails the empty-decode assertion, observed in negative-control.log.
Parsing full payloads during headers-only reads triggers the payload marker guard; dropping or adding identities breaks the exact projected list; the negative control demonstrates this guard firing.
assertion_audit.tests/test_every_ledger_question_reads_t: These checks fail if any reader loses the independently enumerated three identities, reports false membership or discards aggregate version 7; they do not assert derived figure values.

The setup assertions fail if files remain; reverting to file-backed readers makes the post-removal answer differ from the nonempty first answer; both arms at head read the store, so this does not establish document/store field parity.
The setup fails if an aggregate was accidentally created; restoring dependence on an aggregate drops the stored identities and fails the population expectations.
Reverting to file membership omits the extra stored-only id; decoding stored payloads instead of selecting ids raises in the parser instrument.
Preferring the stale document over the store changes the member or population and fails the original-row expectation.
No archive creation breaks the setup; omitting archived rows or their detail breaks identity/detail/membership checks.
Missing initial detail breaks the setup; losing rotated durable identity/member or resurrecting deleted detail fails the independent field checks.
Removing the project predicate decodes the foreign marker and raises; returning foreign rows or dropping local rows fails identity/project checks.
The setup requires no store or directory; reinstating read-time RunStore construction creates them and fails the final absence checks; losing file fallback fails identities.
Returning empty data or raising on the readable schema after clearing metadata fails; this identity assertion alone does not demonstrate the absence of writes under a privileged uid.

Identity loss fails the initial check; sourcing rows outside the deleted store fails the empty middle read; rebuild equality fails a non-idempotent reconstruction, but a consistently dropped field survives because first is its own rebuild input and oracle (finding).

Using the authoritative store as import/compare input reports zero rather than two missing/imported rows; broken import leaves a nonzero comparison; broken cold import misses the three-row count or original full-row equality.

non-blocking: first is produced by ledger.load and then passed back through fill_store(first) before being used as the expected result; a loader that consistently drops a non-identity field passes this equality and the preceding identity-only check, so assert the rebuilt full rows against the original _rows() population as well; the from_documents arm at :165 likewise already reads the store at head and is not an independent document-parity oracle.

reuse_audit._aggregate_headers: Wraps existing load_aggregate and the existing metadata index; does not fork header parsing.
reuse_audit._archive_path: Factors RunStore.archive_path in the owning module; the property delegates to it.
reuse_audit._hydrate: Wraps stored_run_rows for ids selected by the operational index; no independent record retrieval implementation.
reuse_audit._record_rows and nested epoch: Extends the existing _indexed_records join owner; both readers delegate to this one join, and epoch reuses parse_utc.
reuse_audit._store_signature: Combines file_memo.file_signature over the main/archive/WAL files; reuses the existing stat identity owner.
reuse_audit.derived figures: Duplicated capability: ledger.read_records derives the same wall time and width that summary.run_rows already owns; blocking finding.
reuse_audit.search: Searched record retrieval, projection/header loading, timestamp and width derivation, archive naming, stat signatures and hydration in reckon/run_store.py, reckon/ledger.py, reckon/crew/open_run_index.py, reckon/file_memo.py and reckon/crew/summary.py at the reviewed revision; also read the added fixture/helper definitions as test scaffolding for these capabilities.
reuse_audit.stored_run_rows: Read-only selected wrapper around the shared join in the store owner.
reuse_audit.test definitions: Fixtures, readers and parser instruments exercise the store/ledger owners in temporary state; no new production store or decoder is introduced.
